The science moving underneath all of this

IVG: when a cell becomes an option.

In vitro gametogenesis (IVG) is the effort to turn ordinary somatic cells, such as skin or blood cells, into functional eggs or sperm in the laboratory. The process begins by reprogramming those cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), then guiding them through the complex developmental path that normally occurs inside the gonads.

In mice, this has already worked: multiple research groups in Japan and the United States have produced fertile offspring from IVG-derived gametes. Human research is advancing, with several labs and companies now generating early-stage germ cells and, in some cases, immature gametes. Full functional human gametes suitable for reproduction have not yet been achieved.

We simply preserve the cells that future breakthroughs may one day make useful.

01

A cell is taken

IVG begins with an ordinary living cell, typically a skin or blood cell. Not an embryo, not a clinic procedure, not a partner.

02

It is reprogrammed

That cell is reprogrammed into an induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC), the Nobel Prize-winning technique from 2012 the entire field is built on.

03

Options open

What that unlocks over the coming decades is genuinely unknown. Which is precisely the argument for holding a sample rather than not.

No sample, no options. Ever. Every version of this future, whatever form it takes and whatever the law eventually permits, starts from one non-negotiable input: an intact biological sample of a specific person. Preservation is the cheap, boring first step that keeps every later door open, and the one step that cannot be taken retroactively.

You are not buying a descendant. You are buying the right to still be in the conversation when the science arrives.

MySpawn™ performs no cloning, gene editing, IVG, or reproductive services of any kind. We preserve biological material and personal records. Everything above is context, not an offer.

FAQ

The three things people ask the most.

Is my DNA actually safe?
Yes. Your sample is shipped, accessioned, and stored by GenVault, our Biobanking Storage Partner: an ISO 9001 certified, ISO 20387 accredited, CAP accredited and FDA registered US facility operating under the same standards as hospitals and clinical research labs. Barcoded, logged, tracked end-to-end. Your sample lives there, not at MySpawn. So even if our company changes hands, your material is protected.
Can my family access this when I'm gone?
Yes. You designate the people who get access to your vault and the authority to act on your stored sample. The digital and biological version of a will. Built for the future you're actually planning for.
What if descendant creation never becomes legal?
Then you've spent a few hundred dollars on a complete personal vault and a recorded version of yourself for the people who'll love you most. If it does happen, and the curve of biotech progress suggests it will, you're in the vault, ready, and you got there first.
The one step you can't take later

Anything can happen tomorrow. Preserve yourself today.

None of us knows what tomorrow holds. An accident, an illness, a pandemic, a war. Any one of them can close the window for good. A sample can only be taken while you're still here, so the only safe time to preserve it is now.
